approach: Hide and Speak: speech hidden in speech by encoder-decoder networks with differentiable STFT/iSTFT layers
capacity: one to five speech messages in one speech carrier of unchanged dimension; quality falls as the count rises
security_notion: perceptual: a human evaluator should not detect the message; ABX 51.2% against a chance rate of 50%; no steganalysis evaluation
robustness: robust to down-sampling, MP3 and added noise; fails under 8-bit precision reduction
pre_coordination: trained encoder, carrier decoder and message decoder; with several messages, each intended recipient is the only one who can recover theirs
builds_on: Baluja 2017 (Hiding images in plain sight); Zhu et al. 2018 (HiDDeN)
notes: Image deep-hiding architecture carried into speech; vision models applied directly fail after the time-domain round trip (vision-models-fail-on-speech).

approach: Speech hidden in speech (Kreuk et al.)
builds_on: Kreuk et al. 2019
notes: Restates kreuk_2019:approach-hide-and-speak.

approach: Survey and theory of the limits of steganography: unified terminology, attacks, obstacles to a Shannon-style theory, and the practical ideas theory yields
carrier_medium: general covertext (redundant bits after a transform)
channel: other (general model: key-selected subset of redundant bits)
capacity: upper bound: gap between lossy and lossless compression; safe rate may tend to zero as the warden sees more stegotext
security_notion: no formal notion; no theory comparable to Shannon's; security depends on the covertext model
robustness: passive versus active wardens; an active warden with as good a model can replace the redundancy with noise
pre_coordination: shared secret key under Kerckhoffs' assumption
builds_on: Simmons' Prisoners' Problem; Shannon's theory of secrecy systems; historical hiding recounted by Kahn
notes: Contribution node; also proposes the keyed sentence-hash text scheme and the Stego Turing Test (claim sentence-hash-stego-turing-test). Hopper et al. 2002 say their Constructions 1 and 2 can be found in this paper.

approach: Parity embedding: a pad or keystream selects a set of cover elements and each bit is embedded as their parity, changing whichever element is least obtrusive
robustness: larger parity sets let an active warden inject noise more easily
pre_coordination: shared one-time pad or keystream generator
builds_on: the selection-channel argument
notes: General technique; the pixel is the paper's example. The paper says it improves efficiency and enables public-key steganography.
carrier: parity of key-selected cover elements (e.g. image pixels)

approach: Public-key steganography: encrypt under the recipient's public key and embed as block parities; every recipient tries to decrypt; against an active warden a short one-time key permutes the cover bits
carrier_medium: general covertext; broadcast posts (mailing list, usenet) in the active-warden case
security_notion: passive warden cannot tell the pseudorandom parities from plain cover
robustness: possible against an active warden only under a modified Prisoners' Problem
pre_coordination: no shared secret; the recipient's public key is known to the sender
builds_on: the authors' earlier workshop version
notes: key=none because no secret is shared before imprisonment; a session key can then drive a conventional scheme.

approach: Balanced-partition stegosystem: split the covertext alphabet into two parts of near-equal probability and let a one-bit key choose which part carries the bit
capacity: one bit per covertext
security_notion: relative entropy (information-theoretic)
robustness: passive adversary only
pre_coordination: one-bit shared key; covertext distribution known to both
notes: Also presents the one-time pad on uniform covertext. Hopper et al. 2002 call this an information-theoretic version of their stateless protocol.
carrier: choice of covertext from a near-equiprobable half

approach: Information-theoretic model of steganography against a passive adversary: detection as hypothesis testing, security as relative entropy between cover and stego distributions
carrier_medium: covertext as a random variable with known distribution
security_notion: relative entropy D(PC||PS); perfect when zero; error probabilities of any detector bounded by it
robustness: passive adversary only
pre_coordination: secret key shared by Alice and Bob; Eve knows everything else
builds_on: Simmons' Prisoners' Problem
notes: Workshop version; superseded by cachin_2004.

approach: Universal stegosystem: Willems' repetition-times compressor modified to swap a low-probability block for its neighbour in the repetition-time ranking
carrier_medium: source blocks coded by a universal compressor
channel: other (swap of low-probability block with its rank neighbour)
security_notion: asymptotically perfect security claimed; formal statement deferred
robustness: passive adversary only
pre_coordination: shared secret key
builds_on: Willems, universal data compression and repetition times
notes: Replaced in cachin_2004 by a compression-plus-one-time-pad construction.
carrier: source blocks of a repetition-times compressor

approach: Balanced-partition stegosystem for arbitrary known distributions: a one-bit key chooses which of two near-equiprobable halves carries the bit
capacity: one bit per covertext
security_notion: relative entropy; perfect secrecy for the message
robustness: passive adversary only
pre_coordination: one-bit shared key; covertext distribution known
builds_on: the 1998 workshop version
notes: Restates cachin_1998:approach-balanced-partition. Finding the optimal embedding is NP-hard.
carrier: choice of covertext from a near-equiprobable half

approach: Information-theoretic model of steganography against a passive adversary; detection as hypothesis testing; perfect when relative entropy is zero
carrier_medium: covertext as a random variable; the covertext is generated, not modified
security_notion: relative entropy D(PC||PS); binary relative entropy of the error rates bounded by it
robustness: passive adversary only
pre_coordination: random secret key exchanged over a secure channel before use; Kerckhoffs
builds_on: Simmons' Prisoners' Problem; the 1998 workshop version
notes: Journal version of cachin_1998. Notes Hopper et al. as taking up the complexity-theoretic extension.

approach: Perfectly secure stegosystems for uniform covertext: a key-shifted reference to a uniformly likely Bible verse, and the one-time pad on random bits
carrier_medium: Bible-verse references; uniformly random bit strings
channel: other (key-shifted choice of a reference into a shared book)
security_notion: perfect: covertext and stegotext distributions equal
robustness: passive adversary only
pre_coordination: shared uniformly random key; shared copy of the book; covertext distribution known
notes: Bible example combines a shared codebook with a shared key; the paper calls a uniform covertext unrealistic.
carrier: reference to an equally likely item (a Bible verse)

approach: Universal stegosystem: approximate the covertext distribution by universal compression, then generate stegotext from private randomness with the message one-time-padded into the encoder output
carrier_medium: covertext of n independent repetitions of one experiment
capacity: message of up to n H(X) bits
security_notion: secure on average, perfect asymptotically, against a warden who sees a finite part
robustness: passive adversary only
pre_coordination: shared key
builds_on: universal data compression (method of types)
notes: Generates rather than modifies the cover; relies on Alice's private randomness.
carrier: covertext sampled from an estimated distribution

approach: Complexity-theoretic steganography: secrecy and robustness defined by computational indistinguishability; secure and robust protocols exist if one-way functions exist
carrier_medium: any channel: a distribution on timestamped bit sequences
capacity: one hidden bit per channel block
security_notion: computational indistinguishability from the channel (steganographic secrecy)
robustness: robustness against a warden bounded by a relation; an unbounded warden destroys any hidden information
pre_coordination: secret key and synchronised counter
builds_on: Simmons' Prisoners' Problem; information-theoretic models (Cachin and others), which it calls limited
notes: The stegosystem only samples the channel through an oracle; security assumes a perfect oracle, which a human cannot supply.

approach: Construction 4: a keyed PRF picks the maximising n-shingle of each document and an unbiased function of it carries the bit
channel: other (keyed function of the maximising n-shingle of a document)
robustness: survives edits that preserve shingle overlap
pre_coordination: two shared secret keys
notes: First robust text construction in this line; needs encryption whose bit errors commute.
carrier: choice of document, read through its maximising shingle

approach: Construction 1: for each encoded bit draw up to two channel blocks until a keyed PRF of counter and block equals the bit
carrier_medium: any channel, sampled through an oracle
capacity: one bit per block; some failure probability per bit, absorbed by an error-correcting code
security_notion: universal steganographic secrecy, for every channel distribution
pre_coordination: shared secret key and synchronised counter
builds_on: Anderson and Petitcolas 1998 (protocol said to be not new)
notes: Rejection-sampling ancestor of later generative stegosystems; the novelty claimed is the proof.

approach: Construction 2: encrypt with an IND$-CPA cipher, then rejection-sample each block until a public function unbiased on the channel yields the next ciphertext bit
carrier_medium: any channel admitting an unbiased public function
security_notion: steganographic secrecy, assuming a public function unbiased on the channel (a strong assumption)
pre_coordination: shared key
builds_on: Anderson and Petitcolas 1998; Cachin 1998 information-theoretic version
notes: No synchronised state needed.

approach: Construction 3: channel draws from shared pseudorandom inputs replace two shared secret blocks; each bit repeated n times
robustness: robust against any admissible bounding relation; the paper calls it impractical
pre_coordination: shared PRF key and synchronised counter
notes: Existence proof for robust steganography.
carrier: channel draws from shared pseudorandom inputs

approach: Batch capacity theorem: across N covers, secure capacity grows only as the square root of N, proved asymptotically under the shift hypothesis
capacity: secure capacity proportional to the square root of the number of covers
security_notion: Warden hypothesis test with bounded error rates, after Cachin; KL-divergence bound
pre_coordination: number of covers known to both parties in advance
builds_on: Cachin 2004; Ker, Batch steganography and pooled steganalysis
notes: Safe strategy splits the payload equally; bounds orders of magnitude apart.

approach: Square root law for a single cover: batch results carried to one object treated as near-independent regions, tested on spatial and DCT embedding
capacity: secure capacity grows as the square root of cover size, counted in embedding changes
security_notion: detectability under four steganalysis methods; pooled-detector bounds
builds_on: Ker 2007 batch capacity theorem; Anderson 1996 remark on safe rate
notes: A falsifiable but probably unprovable thesis; linear rate only for a steganographer with a perfect cover model.

approach: Subliminal channel: authentication cryptoalgorithms in which several ciphers decrypt to the same message, so the choice of cipher carries hidden bits in full view of the warden
carrier_medium: authenticated ciphertexts on an authentication-without-secrecy channel
channel: other (choice among ciphers that decrypt to the same message)
capacity: one bit per message in the three-prime example; authentication capacity traded bit for bit
security_notion: computational: existence as hard to detect as factoring a product of three primes
robustness: warden cannot detect the channel but can forge accepted messages by forward search
pre_coordination: key chosen in secret from a key list agreed in advance with the warden
builds_on: Simmons's earlier authentication-without-secrecy papers
notes: Origin of the Prisoners' Problem; Simmons's warden is active (impersonation and substitution). The paper says the channel is not coded selection of messages or prearranged code words.
carrier: choice among ciphers that decrypt to the same message

approach: AES-256-GCM ciphertext read as an integer and written as a legal chess game in PGN (mixed-radix over UCI-sorted legal moves), with variation trees
capacity: about 4.3 bits per ply; about 430 bits per 100-move game
security_notion: confidentiality and integrity by AES-GCM; deniability against casual observation only; no detector or proof
robustness: fragile by design: any change to the moves breaks decryption (read as tamper detection)
pre_coordination: key or password and the public algorithm
builds_on: Anderson and Petitcolas 1998, Cachin 1998 (reference list only, not discussed in text)
notes: Move quality plays no part, so cover games need not be plausible play. No model involved, so access_needed is empty.

approach: Code C (bridge): horizontal lead denies a top honour, vertical promises one
capacity: one bit per lead
security_notion: none; detected (83 of 85 leads match, likelihood ratio about 4 x 10^19 at p = 0.9)
pre_coordination: an agreement between partners; opposing declarer unaware
notes: Outside the legal signalling channel of card spots.

approach: Code B (baseball): trash-can bang for a non-fastball sign, silence for a fastball
carrier_medium: trash-can bangs relaying the stolen catcher's sign
capacity: one bit per pitch
security_notion: none; detected (201 of 267 pitches match, likelihood ratio about 3.4 x 10^30 at p = 0.8)
notes: Timing of bangs (between sign and pitch) noted but not modelled.

approach: Action steganography: one RL agent per message symbol; the receiver decodes by classifying which agent produced the episode
carrier_medium: episodes (state trajectories) of agents in a labyrinth
capacity: one bit per trajectory (two agents)
security_notion: Kerckhoffs: adversary knows the system, not the key; passive Eve and active Trudy; steganalyser 0.545 on unseen trajectories
robustness: identifiability near 0.9 up to 0.4 forced-random-action rate, near 0.8 up to 0.7
pre_coordination: shared hyper-parameters and random seeds from which both sides rebuild agents and observer
builds_on: Simmons 1984 prisoners' problem (framing); Cachin 2004 and Hopper et al. 2009 (adversary model)
notes: Stag-hunt framing of cooperation versus optimal overlapping paths.

approach: Chestega: the message is encoded as chess data (positions, pieces, moves, tournaments, players) in chess-related documents, preferably authentic or tool-generated
carrier_medium: chess-related documents: game scripts, training material, analysis, news (PGN)
channel: other (chess-data content: target squares, pieces, players' initials, via an agreed codebook)
capacity: example: 7 bits per move as a target-square index; 4-bit slices as letters via player initials
security_notion: argued resilience to traffic, comparison and linguistic attacks; no formal notion
pre_coordination: agreed configuration (encoding scheme, cover style and type, delivery protocol); no stega-key
builds_on: Graphstega (data rather than noise); criticises Hernandez-Castro et al. 2006
notes: Public method. Uses Chessmaster to generate natural-language analysis.; channel is text about chess, so linguistic-text would also fit
carrier: chess data (squares, pieces, players) in chess-related text

approach: Castle: censorship-circumvention covert channel encoding data as real-time-strategy player actions (unit selections and map targets), executed by desktop automation
carrier_medium: real-time strategy game sessions (0 A.D., Aeons)
channel: other (player action commands: k-of-n unit selection and target map location)
capacity: 50 to 200 B/s generally; about 190 B/s on 0 A.D.; over 400 B/s with tuning
security_notion: resistance to a network censor's traffic analysis (best classifier about 60%); not steganographically secure against an in-game observer
robustness: game's application-layer reliability delivers commands intact
pre_coordination: custom map with immobilised units distributed in advance
builds_on: Rook (game-based covert channel)
notes: Could equally sit under network-covert-channel; security rests on encryption and game passwords.
carrier: unit selections and commands in a real-time strategy game

approach: Comment codebook: synonymous annotations (eight here, three bits) carry the message; any text-steganography technique may apply
capacity: three bits per comment from a set of eight
robustness: low: deleting the comments erases the data
pre_coordination: agreed comment set
builds_on: text steganography generally
notes: Closest published precedent for hiding in chess commentary.
carrier: annotation comments in a game record

approach: Ranked move choice in a new game: shared engine lists moves above threshold T, sorts them by evaluation and plays the i-th to send i
carrier_medium: moves of a newly played game (Go in StegoGo; said to apply to chess and backgammon)
capacity: about log2 of the number of good moves per position; three bits per move in StegoGo
security_notion: statistical; one-sided embedding not detected at 100 games
pre_coordination: identical engine software, parameters and shared secret key
builds_on: Murdoch and Zielinski 2004 equivalent moves
notes: Threshold T trades capacity against invisibility.

approach: Variations inserted into an already played game: bits in where a variant starts, its length and its ranked moves
robustness: erasing all variations removes the data, at a cost to the game file's value
pre_coordination: identical engine software, parameters and shared secret key
notes: Paper calls it simple, high-capacity and secure.
carrier: variations inserted into a played game record

approach: Equivalent-move covert channel: a keyed generator chooses which outcome-equivalent move to play, after frequency hopping, so colluders authenticate one another through moves alone
carrier_medium: Connect-4 moves in an online programming tournament
capacity: one bit (authentication) before the result is fixed; low capacity, high reliability
security_notion: weak: opponents assumed unaware and not adaptive, so cryptanalysis assumed unlikely
robustness: moves arrive intact, but independent players' moves act as noise
pre_coordination: shared key seeding a keyed generator (PRNG)
builds_on: frequency-hopping spread-spectrum radio; multilevel secure systems; Bridge signalling (Winkler 1983)
notes: Move timing considered and rejected (claim move-timing-channel).

approach: General covert-channel framework for combinatorial games: the sender plays, assigns bit strings to her strategy's moves via a keyed permutation of the best moves, and plays the matching one
carrier_medium: move sequences (Tic-Tac-Toe; said to apply to chess and Go)
capacity: up to floor(log2 N) bits per move; reduced but non-zero under perfect play
security_notion: passive warden tests moves against her model of play; outcome set by whose cover model is better
robustness: not addressed (trusted channel, passive adversary)
pre_coordination: shared random number generator and seed
builds_on: Hernandez-Castro et al. 2006; Simmons' Prisoners' Problem
notes: Generalised to multiplayer and imperfect-information games.
carrier: choice among moves the sender's strategies allow

approach: HyperSteg: autoencoder with preparation, hiding and reveal networks that maps message and carrier features onto the Poincaré ball and blends them by Poincaré beta-concatenation
robustness: white-box FGSM and I-FGSM: on average 32.2% more robust than the Euclidean counterpart; near-copy decoders H1-H4 fail to recover the message
builds_on: hyperbolic neural networks (Ganea et al. 2018); Hyperbolic neural networks++ (Shimizu et al. 2021); DeepStego (Baluja 2017); Hide and speak (Kreuk et al. 2020)
notes: The paper names no key; near-copy decoders failing (Claim 9) suggests the trained reveal network acts as one. No detector of carrier presence is tested.

approach: ADV-EMB: distortion-minimisation JPEG steganography whose embedding costs are made asymmetric by the gradient signs of a target CNN steganaliser, on a minimal adjustable subset of elements
carrier_medium: JPEG images (BOSSBase); spatial-domain extension on grayscale images
capacity: 0.1 to 0.5 bpnzAC (JPEG); 0.4 bpp in the spatial extension
security_notion: total error rate (mean of missed detection and false alarm) against supervised steganalysers; adversary-unaware and adversary-aware steganalysts; three iterated rounds
pre_coordination: steganographer needs white-box gradient access to a target steganaliser, which it may build on its own side
builds_on: J-UNIWARD and S-UNIWARD (Holub et al.); Xu-CNN steganaliser; distortion-minimisation framework and syndrome-trellis coding (Filler et al.); ASO; SI-UNIWARD; adversarial examples (Goodfellow et al.); Zhang et al. adversarial cover enhancement
notes: register row is tang_2074 (page number misread as year); CNN gradients set costs, so it sits between classical and deep image steganography

approach: StegaStamp: jointly trained encoder/decoder that adds an RGB residual to a photo to carry a hyperlink bitstring, trained through differentiable print/display-and-camera corruptions
carrier_medium: natural photographs, printed or displayed and re-captured by camera
capacity: 100 encoded bits per image; at least 56 bits after BCH error correction
security_notion: perceptual invisibility enforced by L2, LPIPS and a Wasserstein critic loss; no steganalysis evaluation
robustness: physical transmission: perspective warp, blur, colour shifts, noise, JPEG; 98.7% mean bit-accuracy over 18 printer/display-camera combinations; tolerates partial occlusion
pre_coordination: encoder and decoder trained together; receiver needs the trained decoder and detector
builds_on: HiDDeN (Zhu et al. 2018); Light Field Messaging; Expectation over Transformation (Athalye et al.); Shin and Song JPEG approximation; BiSeNet; BCH codes
notes: tancik_2020 is a byte-identical copy of this file; residual sometimes visible in flat regions

approach: SteganoGAN: adversarially trained dense encoder hides an arbitrary bit tensor in a cover image; decoder recovers it
capacity: up to 4.4 RS-bpp (Reed–Solomon-corrected); 2 bpp while Ye-net auROC stays at or below 0.8
security_notion: Only sender and receiver should detect presence; StegExpose auROC 0.59; detector that knows the algorithm but not the weights struggles
pre_coordination: Receiver holds the trained decoder; trained on Div2K or COCO
builds_on: DenseNet; Hayes & Danezis 2017; Baluja 2017; HiDDeN (zhu_2018); HUGO (Pevný et al. 2010); Ye et al. 2017 steganalyser; Reed–Solomon codes
notes: Comparison with WOW, S-UNIWARD and HILL used figures from a different dataset

approach: Adversarial architecture: a steganalyser trained in the loop, a three-player game
security_notion: steganalyser as discriminator in training; does not guarantee resistance to an independently trained steganalyser
builds_on: Hayes and Danezis 2017; Shang et al. 2020; Xu et al. 2016; Ye et al. 2017; Weng et al. 2019
notes: Security target: the steganalyser does no better than a random guess.

approach: Cover-dependent deep hiding with a preparation network (Baluja)
capacity: 24 bpp (a full-size colour image in another of the same size)
security_notion: easily detected: SRNet detection accuracy 99.58% on Baluja 2017
builds_on: Baluja 2017; Baluja 2019
notes: Survey's account, not the original paper's.

approach: Cover-dependent deep hiding without a preparation network
builds_on: Weng et al. 2019; Mishra et al. 2019; Zhang et al. 2020a; Baluja 2019
notes: The survey's default architecture. SRNet accuracies of 77.43% (Weng 2019), 75.69% (Lu 2021), 75.54% (Guan 2022) and 55.86% (HiNet) in srnet-detection-rates belong to schemes in this broad class.

approach: Light field messaging: hidden data sent screen-to-camera
carrier_medium: images displayed on a screen and photographed
security_notion: no concern for steganalysis
robustness: robustness to display and camera distortion is the goal
builds_on: Wengrowski and Dana 2019; Tancik et al. 2020 (StegaStamp); Jia et al. 2020 (RIHOOP); Zhang et al. 2020a
notes: Also termed photographic steganography.
carrier: images shown on a screen and photographed

approach: Universal deep hiding (UDH): secret encoded independently of the cover, added to any cover
builds_on: Zhang et al. 2020a
notes: Cover-independent encoding; the survey also credits it with watermarking efficiency and light-field robustness.

approach: HiDDeN: encoder and decoder trained end-to-end with an adversary, and noise layers between them for robustness; message replicated spatially into the encoder
capacity: 0.203 bpp (52 bits per 16×16 patch), bit error below 1e-5
security_notion: Adversary cannot tell whether an image carries a message; ATS detection 50% when weights are unknown, 98% when known
robustness: Trained noise layers (dropout, cropout, crop, Gaussian, differentiable JPEG) give robustness; worse than Digimarc against frequency-domain noise
pre_coordination: Receiver holds the trained decoder; blind decoding without the cover
builds_on: Hayes & Danezis 2017 ([21]); adversarial examples (Goodfellow et al., Szegedy et al.); HUGO, WOW and S-UNIWARD baselines; ATS steganalyser; Digimarc
notes: Same framework also used for watermarking (family watermarking applies as well)

approach: Steganography without embedding via DCGAN: secret bits mapped to the generator's noise vector; a trained extractor recovers it
capacity: σ bits per noise value, 3×|z| bits per image; 9.16e-3 bytes/pixel; recovery accuracy about 0.89–0.96, not 100%
security_notion: Warder must not detect presence; stego equals cover by construction; detection low unless the steganalyser trains on the same image set, so security rests on keeping the training set secret
pre_coordination: Sender holds trained generator G, receiver holds trained extractor E trained for that G; both agree the interval mapping (σ, δ)
builds_on: Goodfellow GANs; DCGAN (Radford et al.); earlier SWE by cover selection (Zhou et al., bag-of-words, image hashing) and cover synthesis (texture); Hayes & Danezis 2017 for accuracy comparison
notes: Detection accuracies rise to 0.56/0.98/0.74 when the steganalysers train on the method's own image set

approach: Method.9: average pixel values of sub-images hashed; secret segmented by Chinese sentence structure against a dictionary
channel: other (cover selection by average-pixel hash with dictionary)
builds_on: Zou et al. 2019 (survey ref [41])

approach: Method.2: bag-of-words visual words mapped to text keywords; sub-images selected to express the text
pre_coordination: Hash function and position tag sequence agreed in advance; shared mapping between visual words and keywords
builds_on: Zhou, Cao and Sun 2016, bag-of-words coverless hiding (survey ref [20])

approach: Method.7: secret mapped to a DCGAN noise vector; extractor recovers it
security_notion: Survey: attacker without the same GAN model cannot extract
pre_coordination: Sender owns G, receiver owns E
builds_on: Hu et al. 2018 (ledgered hu_2018; Restates edge)
notes: Survey Section III-G runs SGAN (Volkhonskiy et al.) together with Hu et al.; survey gives 9.16e-3 as bits per pixel where hu_2018 says bytes per pixel

approach: Method.10: DCT DC-coefficient feature sequences within LDA topic classes
channel: other (cover selection by DCT feature sequence)
builds_on: Zhang, Peng and Long 2018 (survey ref [42])

approach: Method.11: block matching with DenseNet semantic features and DC-coefficient hashes
builds_on: Luo et al. 2019 (survey ref [43]); Method.8

approach: Method.3: GIF extension attributes classified into categories and mapped to bits
channel: other (cover selection by GIF extension attributes)
builds_on: Ruan and Qin 2017 (survey ref [36])
notes: Survey says capacity grows with the number of attribute dimensions (not quoted in ledger)

approach: Method.1: cover selection by gray-value block hash with an inverted index (8 bits per image)
carrier_medium: image (natural images from a prepared database)
capacity: 8 bits per image
security_notion: Unmodified images leave no modification trace for steganalysis; survey reports Method.1 resists the Pairs method where 0.1 bpp LSB does not
pre_coordination: Sender prepares a large image database and index in advance
builds_on: Zhou et al. 2016 ("Coverless image steganography without embedding", survey ref [33])
notes: Capacity bounded by hash length; longer hashes need a larger database

approach: Method.4: HOG-based block hashes with a two-level inverted index; shared block position shifted per transmission
pre_coordination: HOG hashing algorithm and block position P shared beforehand
builds_on: Zhou et al. 2017 HOG hashing (survey ref [35])

approach: Method.8: partial-duplicate natural images retrieved per patch of a secret image; patches stitched back
channel: other (cover selection by partial-duplicate patch retrieval)
pre_coordination: Patch location information shared as a secret key
builds_on: Zhou, Mu and Wu 2018 (survey ref [21])
notes: Transmits an approximate secret image, not bits

approach: Method.5: SIFT-orientation robust hash (18 bits per image); side information hidden in one extra image by LSB
channel: other (cover selection by SIFT hash, plus LSB side channel)
capacity: 18 bits per image
builds_on: Zheng et al. 2017 robust image hashing (survey ref [37])
notes: One transmitted image is LSB-modified, so the scheme is not wholly modification-free

approach: Method.6: a database of WGAN models turns a secret image into an unrelated-looking image and back
security_notion: Survey: attacker without the same GAN model cannot extract; GAN methods do not guarantee image integrity and quality
pre_coordination: Sender and receiver share the same data set and parameters
builds_on: Duan and Song 2018 (survey ref [39]); WGAN (Arjovsky et al.)
notes: Transmits images, not arbitrary bits

approach: Generative steganography network: StyleGAN2-based generator with a secret block writes secret data into feature maps during generation; same generator makes ordinary covers
capacity: 1–8 bpp; extraction accuracy 97.5% at 1 bpp, about 59–61% at 8 bpp
security_notion: Generated cover and stego indistinguishable to a trained steganalyser (Pe near 0.5; SR-net and Ye-net AUC 0.47–0.54); mutual information between secret and image maximised
robustness: Lossless channel assumed (PNG); small Gaussian noise added in training
pre_coordination: Receiver holds the trained extractor; generator trained jointly with extractor, discriminator and steganalyser
builds_on: StyleGAN2; InfoGAN; SR-net; compared with Hu et al. 2018 (hu_2018), GSS (zhang_2018), Liu ACGAN labels, Zhang 2020 cover synthesis, Yu et al. 2021 attention GAN; HiDDeN (zhu_2018) and SteganoGAN (zhang_2019) as cover-based baselines
notes: Security tested against a steganalyser separating generated covers from generated stegos, not real images from stegos

approach: CRoSS: coverless image steganography by DDIM-inversion translation between a secret image and a container image, using two conditions on a pre-trained Stable Diffusion as private and public keys; no training
capacity: one secret image per container image
security_notion: naturalness (NIQE) plus resistance to learned steganalysers (XuNet, YedroudjNet, KeNet, SID retrained on leaked samples, StegExpose); informal argument that wrong private keys yield plausible decoys
robustness: zero-shot robustness to Gaussian noise, JPEG, WeChat round trip and screen photography; revealed image is semantically, not pixel-exactly, faithful
pre_coordination: sender and receiver share the same pre-trained conditional diffusion model and the private key (prompt, LoRA or ControlNet condition); public key may be guessed from the container

approach: Bins (Fang et al. 2017): shared random partition of the vocabulary into 2^k equal bins; each token's bin carries a k-bit ciphertext block

approach: VLC (Yang et al. 2018): Huffman code over the vocabulary rebuilt at each step from the LM distribution; ciphertext bits walk the tree to a token

notes: Analysed by Dai and Cai, not proposed by them. key=shared-model from the decoder rerunning the same LM (Claim 8).
